title: Confocal Imaging of Live Larval Zebrafish for Assessing Peripheral Neuropathy
author: Sandra Rieger
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.8i2huge

steps.title: Select and anesthetize larvae
steps.instruction: Identify fluorescent larvae under a fluorescent stereomicroscope, add a few drops of tricaine stock to the dish containing the larvae, wait until they are anesthetized, and confirm anesthesia by gently touching each larva with a pipette tip; if no response, transfer the larvae to a small petri dish containing tricaine working solution.

substeps.instruction: Add a few drops of tricaine stock to the larvae dish.
Wait until larvae are anesthetized.
Touch larvae with a pipette tip to assess anesthesia.
If no response, move larvae to a petri dish with tricaine working solution.

steps.title: Embed larvae in low‑melt agarose
steps.instruction: Using a glass Pasteur pipette, transfer each anesthetized larva (one at a time) from the petri dish into a 1.5 ml tube that contains 1.2 % low‑melt agarose kept at 42 °C in a heat block to remain liquid.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 1.2 % low‑melt agarose and keep it at 42 °C.
Place 1.5 ml tube with the warm agarose near the petri dish.
Transfer one anesthetized larva at a time into the tube.

steps.title: Mount larvae in imaging chamber
steps.instruction: Transfer a drop of the agarose‑containing larva into the imaging chamber, immediately orient the larva on its side for lateral view or on its back for dorsal view, immerse the immobilized embryo in tricaine working solution, and seal the chamber—using a lid for a glass‑bottom dish or a frosted slide with silicon grease on the Teflon ring for a Teflon chamber—ensuring no air bubbles remain.

substeps.instruction: Place a drop of agarose with the larva into the imaging chamber.
Position the larva on its side (lateral view) or on its back (dorsal view).
Immerse the mounted larva in tricaine working solution.
Cover with a lid (glass‑bottom dish) or seal with a frosted slide and silicon grease (Teflon chamber).
Check that no air bubbles are trapped after sealing.

steps.title: Configure confocal microscope settings
steps.instruction: On the inverted microscope, select the PlanNeofluar 20x/0.50 (Zeiss) air objective, set a 1.6× digital zoom, and use a 473 nm diode laser to excite GFP‑expressing axons.

substeps.instruction: Choose PlanNeofluar 20x/0.50 air objective.
Apply 1.6× digital zoom.
Select 473 nm diode laser for GFP excitation.

steps.title: Acquire and process image stacks
steps.instruction: Record image stacks by capturing 3 µm optical sections, project each stack into a single image, export the projected images as TIFF files, and then either edit them in Adobe Photoshop for publication or load the original stacks into Imaris software and use the Filament Tracer module to quantify axon debris and axon density.

substeps.instruction: Capture 3 µm sections to build a stack.
Project the stack into a single image.
Export the projected image as a TIFF file.
Optionally process TIFFs in Adobe Photoshop.
Alternatively, import stacks into Imaris and run Filament Tracer for quantitative analysis.
